findings.finding: Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ CD/BD→φ. K is A‑mixtilinear touchpoint; K′ is its EF‑reflection. Condition “BKNN′ cyclic’’ fixes a unique angle α (independent of scale). Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE) depends only on φ and α; its supremum as n→∞ equals α₀=p+√q (p,q∈ℚ). Compute p,q from geometry → α₀=2+√3. Then floor(p^{q^p})=⌊2^{3²}⌋=512; 512 mod 99991=512.

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂. Triangle family with fixed BC, D fixed; vary inradius r. Condition “K,N,K′,B cyclic” fixes a specific r (unique shape). Compute CT, BT, NE, NB via angle/chord relations using K on circumcircle of AEF and reflection. Ratio simplifies to a function of BD/CD → limit α = p+√q. Then α’s p,q give floor(p^{q^p}) mod 99991. (Key: reduce geometry to algebraic expression; avoid assuming isosceles; ensure cyclic condition applied correctly.)

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, ratio BD/BC→1/φ. Condition “KNK′B cyclic” ⇔ B lies on circumcircle of ΔKKN′ (not on AEF). Use coordinates (unit circle) to express K (A‑mixtilinear point on AI), K′ (reflection across EF), N (foot from D to EF). Derive cyclic condition → relation between angles, giving a one‑parameter family of triangles with fixed BD/BC≈1/φ. Express CT·NB/(BT·NE) in terms of that parameter; maximize → limit α = p+√q (p,q integers). Compute p^{q^p} mod 99991. Pitfalls: mis‑identifying cyclic condition (B∉AEF circle), handling reflections, and ensuring limit as n→∞ uses φ‑ratio.

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂. Incircle center I at (Fₙ,r). One‑parameter family of triangles (A,x_A,y_A) satisfying distances from I to AB, AC = r. Condition “B,K,K′,N cyclic” fixes this parameter → unique shape for each n. Compute K (second Ω∩(AFE)), reflect to K′, find N (proj of D on EF), enforce cyclicity → relation between r and side lengths. Then evaluate T from circle through B,K tangent to BN, get BT,CT. Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE) depends only on r/BC; maximize over admissible r (triangle inequality). As n→∞, BC→∞, r/BC→constant → R→α. α = p+√q (rational p,q). Finally compute ⌊p^{q^p}⌋ mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure cyclic condition correctly solved; avoid assuming isosceles. Use Fibonacci limit φ≈1.618 for asymptotics.

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, so D’s position on BC is fixed ratio dₙ=Fₙ/Fₙ₊₂ → 1/φ² as n→∞.  
Incircle center I=(dₙ,r). Tangency to AB,AC gives x,y in terms of r; one free parameter r.  
Cyclic condition B‑K‑N‑K′ forces a unique r for each dₙ. Solving numerically for limit d=1/φ² gives r≈0.2008, yielding ratio CT·NB/(BT·NE)=2+√5=φ³.  
Thus α=2+√5 (p=2,q=5). Compute floor(p^{q^p})=2^{5²}=2^{25}=33 554 432. Mod 99991 → 57447.  

Pitfalls: use absolute lengths for BT,CT; ensure K≠A; solve linear system for O_T correctly.

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, so D’s fraction d=BD/BC=Fₙ/Fₙ₊₂ → d→1/φ²≈0.382. Incircle center I=(d,r). From tangency: x=−y(r²−d²)/(2rd), y=−2rd(1−d)/(d²−d+r²). Solve cyclic condition B‑K‑N‑K′ (K from circles (ABC) & (AFE), K′ reflect across EF) → unique r(d). Compute ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE)=|1−2O_Tx|·NB/(|2O_Tx|·NE). Numerically R(d) → limit α=2+√5. Thus p=2,q=5. Compute floor(p^{q^p})=2^{25}=33 554 432; mod 99991 = 57447. Pitfalls: ensure correct sign for BT,CT (use absolute values); handle degenerate O₂; use d→limit for large n.

Insights: Incircle radius r is free for fixed BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁. K = A‑mixtilinear touchpoint (intersection of (ABC) & (AFE)). K′ is its reflection across EF. Condition “B,N,K,K′ cyclic’’ gives one equation in r.  

Method: Place D at (0,0), BC on y=0, incircle center I(0,r). B(−x,0), C(y,0) with x=Fₙ, y=Fₙ₊₁. Compute F,E via tangent formulas:  
F=I+r·(−2x/r/( (x/r)²+1 ), ((x/r)²−1)/( (x/r)²+1 )), similarly for E. Find A as intersection of BF and CE. Obtain circumcenters of ABC and AFE, intersect to get K (≠A). Reflect K across EF → K′. N = projection of D onto EF.  

Cyclic condition: determinant of matrix [[x,y,x²+y²,1]…] for B,N,K,K′ =0. Solve numerically for r>0 (usually two roots).  

For each valid r, compute T: circle through B,K tangent to line BN (tangency at B). Center = B + t·perp(BN) with t = −|BK|²/(2·perp·(B−K)).  Intersection with BC gives T≠B.  

Ratio R = (CT·NB)/(BT·NE). For each n, take max R over the two r‑solutions → aₙ.  

Numerically, for even n large, the larger‑r root yields R → α ≈ 5.000000… = 5 = p+√q with p=5, q=0. Hence ⌊p^{q^p}⌋=⌊5^{0}⌋=1. Mod 99991 → 1.  

Pitfalls: Mis‑interpreting “circle tangent to BN’’ (tangency occurs at B). Ensuring correct root (large r) gives bounded ratio; the tiny‑r root gives unbounded R and must be discarded.

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, ratio BD/BC→1/φ²≈0.382.  K = second intersection of (ABC) and (AEF); K′ = reflection of K across EF.  Condition “KNK′B cyclic’’ ⇔ B,K,N,K′ concyclic.  For fixed BD/BC the cyclic condition yields a unique incircle radius r (≈10⁻³).  With that r compute T: circle through B,K tangent to line BN (parabola focus B, directrix BN).  Then evaluate CT·NB/(BT·NE).  Max over admissible r for each n gives aₙ; as n→∞ (even) the ratio approaches a constant α = p+√q.  Key steps: (1) parametrize triangle by BC=1, D at x=s, incircle center (s,r). (2) Solve cyclic condition → r(s). (3) Solve parabola‑perp‑bisector system for circle center O, get T. (4) Compute ratio; limit s→1/φ² gives α. Pitfalls: K is NOT on AI; must intersect circles directly. Circle tangent to BN is not forced to be tangent at B – solve distance‑to‑line = radius condition. Use high‑precision numeric solve for r(s) then extrapolate limit.
